skill.name: shadcn
skill.description: Guides AI agents through shadcn/ui project inspection, component discovery, installation, updates, presets, styling, forms, composition, registries, and chat interfaces.
skill.summary: Build and maintain shadcn/ui interfaces with project-aware CLI workflows and component rules.
skill.author: shadcn

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives from Markdown, TSX templates, accessibility attributes, documentation links, and relative references. The skill legitimately runs an unpinned shadcn CLI, retrieves remote registry content, and can modify project files. No prompt injection, credential theft, covert persistence, or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill executes the mutable shadcn@latest package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version, or require confirmation before first execution and upgrades.

remediation.issue: Project metadata is collected automatically during context injection.
remediation.suggestion: Request confirmation and disclose which project metadata enters model context before running info --json.

remediation.issue: Community registry content can enter the project.
remediation.suggestion: Validate registry URLs and require dry-run, diff review, and explicit approval before installation.

remediation.issue: Preset and overwrite workflows can replace local files.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval immediately before apply, init --force, or overwrite operations, and preserve a recoverable diff.

content.value_statement: Building consistent shadcn interfaces requires current project context and correct component APIs. This skill guides discovery, installation, updates, styling, composition, and registry workflows.
actual_capabilities: Reads shadcn project context, including framework, aliases, package manager, preset, and installed components.
Searches configured and community registries for components and blocks.
Retrieves component documentation, examples, and API references before implementation.
Previews registry changes with dry-run, diff, and view workflows.
Guides preset inspection, application, merging, and partial theme or font updates.
Applies rules for forms, composition, styling, icons, accessibility, and chat interfaces.
limitations: Requires a project environment that can run the shadcn CLI.
CLI commands may access networks, install dependencies, or modify project files.
Community registry quality and trust must be evaluated separately.
Project-specific visual requirements still require user direction.

use_cases.title: Implement application screens
use_cases.description: Compose forms, dashboards, dialogs, and chat interfaces from compatible shadcn components.

use_cases.title: Maintain a design system
use_cases.description: Enforce semantic tokens, component composition, icon rules, and accessible interaction patterns.

use_cases.title: Review component updates
use_cases.description: Inspect upstream differences and preserve local changes before approving updates.

prompt_templates.title: Add a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a shadcn button. Inspect project context, confirm installation status, fetch current documentation, and use the existing icon library.

prompt_templates.title: Build a validated form
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a profile form with accessible validation and notification controls. Use installed components, semantic tokens, and project aliases.

prompt_templates.title: Update customized components
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the dialog component while preserving local changes. Preview every affected file, compare differences, and request approval before overwriting.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a preset safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the current preset with this preset code. Explain overwrite, partial, merge, and skip effects before changing any files.

output_examples.input: Create a profile settings form with email validation and notification toggles.
output: A project-aware component plan using FieldGroup and Field.
Accessible validation states using data-invalid and aria-invalid.
Independent notification controls selected from existing shadcn components.

output_examples.input: Update the button component without losing local styling changes.
output_examples.output: A dry-run summary, per-file difference review, and a proposed merge that preserves local modifications before approval.

output_examples.input: Switch this project to a new preset code.
output_examples.output: A comparison of overwrite, partial, merge, and skip outcomes, followed by the approved migration workflow.

best_practices: Run project inspection before choosing imports, package commands, or component APIs.
Use dry-run and diff before updating files with local modifications.
Confirm the registry and review downloaded files before accepting community components.
anti_patterns: Do not guess component APIs without reading current documentation.
Do not overwrite customized components or apply presets without explicit approval.
Do not hardcode aliases, icon libraries, raw colors, or primitive-specific properties.

faq.question: Does this skill modify project files?
faq.answer: Yes. Add, apply, init, and dependency commands can change files. Review previews and approve destructive operations.

faq.question: Does this skill require internet access?
faq.answer: Usually. The CLI may download packages, registry content, documentation, examples, and preset data.

faq.question: Can it preserve customized components?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports dry-run and difference workflows for reviewing upstream changes before merging.

faq.question: Does it support Base UI and Radix?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads the project base and applies matching APIs and trigger patterns.

faq.question: Can it use community registries?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify the registry, inspect downloaded files, and verify imports, dependencies, and composition.

faq.question: Does it replace product design decisions?
faq.answer: No. It enforces implementation rules, but visual direction, requirements, and acceptance decisions remain with the user.
